question: Should `tool-progress` become a permanent public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-payload` contract, or should this Slack/Codex fix keep the signal internal pending a separately designed progress API?
rationale: The PR solves a real delivery bug, but the chosen cross-boundary mechanism adds a lasting third-party Plugin SDK API; repository policy and current discussion do not establish maintainer approval for that product/API direction.

options.title: Keep Signal Internal
options.body: Use a closed internal reply-payload marker for this fix and defer public progress API design to a separately reviewed contract change.

options.title: Approve Public Contract
options.body: Keep the new public constant and predicate, document supported producer and channel semantics, and add focused compatibility coverage before merge.

recommendation.title: Keep Signal Internal
recommendation.body: Use a closed internal reply-payload marker for this fix and defer public progress API design to a separately reviewed contract change.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across the affected Slack, reply-payload, and Codex surfaces and is the best available owner for the cross-boundary API choice.
